newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sabvest amends terms of restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Sabvest amends terms of restructuring.

text.p: Industrial holding company Sabvest Ltd announced on Thursday that it had amended the terms of its proposed restructuring following the sale of shares by subsidiary Merhold Investment Corp.
It said that Merhold had sold all of its 2.587 million Primedia Ltd "N" combined units at a slightly higher than expected price.

The sale of the shares realised a net amount of about 41.5 million rand, which resulted in a gain over carrying value before revaluation of about 34.5 million rand and a gain on valuation for net asset value purposes at June 30 1996 of 2.7 million rand.
The proceeds of sale were used to reduce Merhold's interest bearing borrowings to under five million rand.
As a result of this transaction, Sabvest said that Merhold shareholders would now receive 125 Sabvest "N" shares for every 100 held, compared to the 120 Sabvest "N" shares initially offered.
The company said that other than the financial effects of the disposal on the Sabvest group and the revised Merhold exchange ratio, there were no material changes to the proposed restructuring.
Sabhold Group Ltd minority shareholders would still receive 210 Sabvest N shares for every 100 Sabhold shares held by them, it said.
The company said on September 12 that the restructuring of the group, which is still subject to court approval, would result in the delisting of Sabhold and Merhold.
